subject: Agriculture
title: Mycorrhizal Fungi
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Mycorrhizal Fungi.

hook.text: Plant roots are too thick to reach most soil nutrients. Fungi threads are a thousand times thinner—and they share.

buildup.text: Mycorrhizal fungi attach to roots and extend hair-thin hyphae deep into soil to absorb phosphorus and water.

discovery.text: The plant pays the fungus in sugar from photosynthesis. The fungus pays the plant in minerals. Fair trade.

twist.text: Over 90% of land plants depend on mycorrhizae. Without them, most crops grow poorly or not at all.

climax.text: Tilling and chemical fertilizer reduce mycorrhizae. No-till farming and cover crops help them recover.

punchline.text: Plants don't feed themselves. Fungi do the grocery shopping.

quiz.question: What do mycorrhizal fungi provide to plant roots?
options: Phosphorus and water in exchange for plant sugars

details.summary: Mycorrhizal fungi form symbiotic relationships with over 90% of plant species, extending root systems by up to 100 times and dramatically improving nutrient and water uptake. This topic covers arbuscular and ectomycorrhizal types, how the symbiosis works, and why it matters for farming.
details.whyItMatters: Mycorrhizal networks are nature's nutrient delivery system. They transport phosphorus, zinc, and water to crops in exchange for plant sugars. Tillage and high-phosphorus fertilization disrupt these networks, reducing their benefits in conventional.
takeaways: Mycorrhizal fungi colonize plant roots and extend the nutrient-gathering network up to 100x
They provide phosphorus, zinc, and water in exchange for plant-produced sugars
Tillage and excessive phosphorus fertilization suppress mycorrhizal colonization

faq.question: How do mycorrhizal fungi help crop plants?
faq.answer: Mycorrhizal hyphae extend far beyond root reach into soil pores too small for roots to access. They absorb phosphorus, zinc, copper, and water and transport them to the plant in exchange for up to 20% of the plant's photosynthetic sugars. They also help protect roots from pathogens.

faq.question: Why do modern farming practices often reduce mycorrhizal benefits?
faq.answer: Tillage physically severs mycorrhizal networks. High phosphorus fertilization eliminates the plant's need to invest in fungal partners. Fungicide applications can kill mycorrhizae. Fallow periods without living roots starve the fungi. No-till and cover cropping preserve mycorrhizal networks.
